newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grain group sees higher China corn output.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain group sees higher China corn output.

text.p: China was experiencing significantly better corn-growing conditions than last year, members of a U.S. Feed Grains Council (USFGC) delegation said Monday after returning from a crop tour there.
USFGC staff and grain industry representatives toured the northeastern provinces of Jilin and Heilongjiang, which accounted for 24 percent of China's 1995 corn production.

Todd Meyer, director of USFGC's China office, said 1996 corn production area in Jilin was 2.48 million hectares, up 5.8 percent from 1995. He said Jilin's production was pegged at 17.1 million tonnes, up 14 percent from 1995.

Similarly in Heilongjiang, the area planted to corn was 2.67 million hectares, up 10.5 percent from 1995. Meyer said the province's expected minimum crop was 14.03 million tonnes, up about 15 percent from last year.

"According to provincial officials, Jilin and Heilongjiang will add four million tonnes over last year's corn production," Meyer said in a statement. "Overall, that means the crop should be average or better."

"Most of the trade and many officials we spoke with expect that China will enter the export market to some degree in the coming year. Remaining old stocks, a good new crop and stable prices are all evidence in support of exports," Meyer said.
"The quantity is likely to be small -- less than one mmt (million metric ton or million tonne)... but some observers put the level up to about three mmt," he said.
In 1995 Jilin yielded 6.4 tonnes per hectare and Heilongjiang yielded 5.0 tonnes per hectare.
Traders representing such companies as Continental Grain Company, Louis Dreyfus Co and Toepfer International also participated in the tour.
